name: Qatari Nationality by Naturalisation, Marriage Ground (Law No. 38 of 2005, Article 8)

requirement_groups.name: Standard route -- foreign wife of a Qatari man

requirements.blocker_text: Married to a Qatari man. NOTE: Qatari law provides no equivalent citizenship-by-marriage route for a foreign man married to a Qatari woman -- see the structural note below.
Marriage maintained 5+ years from the marriage announcement date. Eligibility is retained even if widowed or divorced before the 5 years complete, provided she continued residing in Qatar.
requirements.fix_path: Remain married (or continue residing in Qatar if widowed/divorced) for 5 years from the marriage announcement.

evidence_required.document: Proof of continued residence in Qatar

sources.title: American University in Cairo, Center for Migration and Refugee Studies -- verbatim English translation of Law No. 38 of 2005, Article 8: foreign wife of a Qatari man may acquire nationality after 5 years of marriage from the announcement date; retains eligibility if widowed/divorced before completion provided continued Qatar residence; Article 10: Qatari women do not lose nationality upon marrying a non-Qatari

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Qatar). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2 sourcing caveat as qa_citizenship_naturalisation.json (academic translation of primary text, Al Meezan's own tier-1 page unreachable in this build). GENDERED STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY, CONFIRMED NOT ASSUMED: this citizenship-by-marriage route exists ONLY for a foreign woman married to a Qatari man. There is NO equivalent provision letting a foreign man married to a Qatari woman acquire citizenship by marriage -- he is instead limited to the 2018 Permanent Residency law's exemption category for 'non-Qatari husbands of Qatari women' (see qa_permanent_residence.json's exempt_category group), which grants settled status, not citizenship. This is a real and durable asymmetry in the primary legal text, not folk knowledge or an assumption. dual_citizenship_allowed is FALSE, consistent with Qatar's general no-dual-citizenship rule for naturalised citizens outside the Article 6 discretionary exception.
